chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked him about the salat of the two 'Eids, and he said: They are two rak'ahs; there is nothing before them and nothing after them.

key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: the two 'Eids, meaning 'Eid al-Fitr and 'Eid al-Adha
key_terms.بَعْدَهُمَا: after them, meaning after the 'Eid prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَتَانِ: two rak'ahs, the prescribed number of units for this prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةِ: salat (prayer), referring here to the ritual prayer of the two 'Eids
key_terms.قَبْلَهُمَا: before them, meaning before the 'Eid prayer

ai.seo_question: How many rak'ahs are in the salat of the two 'Eids, and is there any prayer before or after it?
ai.summary: This hadith states the ruling for the salat of the two 'Eids, specifying that it consists of two rak'ahs. It also indicates that there are no prayers prescribed before it or after it in this context.
